chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: Chick Webb the drummer who could not read
summary: Webb had more imagination than ten drummers, phrased arrangements perfectly without reading, and could hum any soloist's chorus.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: So he had all those great musicians, like I told you, Johnny Hodges and Cootie Williams. He was with Chick before Duke.
: Is that so? I didn't know that.
That's right. That's where Duke got him, from Chick Webb.
: I remember Chick. He was a little hunchbacked man, right?
Yeah, but what a drummer. What a drummer. He had more imagination than ten drummers.
And a lot of drummers copied him, too,

And Chick couldn't read a note. But Chick could -- You would play an arrangement and Chick could phrase that arrangement like he had just played it just the last time you ran it down. He could phrase the arrangement, knew how to crescendo, the crescendos and decrescendos, and I tell you something else about Chick. You could play a solo and he'll come out of the bandstand and come to you and hum every note you played that whole solo.
